source_snapshot.procedure: Enable BIOS debug/error injection, deploy ITP, halt, call parameterless ei.injectMCERR(), resume and collect evidence.
source_snapshot.criteria: Crash/hang then eventual reboot, BMC CPU Catastrophic Error, fault light, recovered UEFI fatal event and optional LCD CPU Over Temp.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; delegates injection but proposes incomplete post-event SSH/dmesg and SEL tails.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; the parameterless target, per-socket coverage, outage timing, event map and recovery are unresolved.

old_problem: Items require Socket 0~N, but `injectMCERR()` accepts no socket argument and its implicit selection/broadcast behavior is undocumented. `Eventually` and the CPU Over Temp mapping also leave timing and PASS semantics indeterminate.
disposition_reason: The MCERR purpose and named Intel action are identifiable, so the case remains package/user-confirmed rather than intrinsically BLOCKED. ED-16 requires approved harness semantics, isolation, deterministic oracle and recovery. The parameterless target behavior controls both blast radius and Socket 0~N coverage and cannot be guessed or treated as a simple runtime value under ED-03.
decision_basis: Directly read XLSX Reliability rows 10 and 11 with exact commands, Criteria and DeepSeek fields.
Read historical record 2416 and preserved source identity and hashes.
Do not invent a socket argument or assume active-context versus broadcast behavior for `injectMCERR()`.
An external timeline is required because SSH can be unavailable during the intended crash/hang.
The LCD over-temperature text requires an approved MCERR event-map justification.
No BIOS, ITP, injection, reset, power, retry or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Intel MCERR catastrophic-path validation with verified implicit target
test_case.purpose: Inject MCERR once for every required socket using the harness's authoritative target-selection mechanism and verify the complete catastrophic outage, autonomous recovery and affected-CPU evidence.
required_package: Board/CPU socket topology and authoritative parameterless target/broadcast semantics
Approved ITP/CScripts build/hash and per-socket coverage method
Independent-console recovery and BIOS restoration procedure
test_case.test_command: A qualified Intel FAE on a dedicated SUT must prove the active/implicit target before each authorized `ei.injectMCERR()` call, record the package context, perform one injection, monitor the crash/hang and autonomous reboot externally, capture complete MCERR/catastrophic evidence after recovery, and restore all debug settings. Do not add an invented socket argument or count a broadcast/implicit result as all-socket coverage without authority.
test_case.expected_result: Each approved socket is demonstrably targeted exactly as specified; the platform follows the signed crash/hang-to-autonomous-reboot timing and produces the exact affected-CPU MCERR/catastrophic records and applicable indicators, followed by healthy recovery and full setting restoration.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires authoritative target proof and complete per-socket coverage, bounded timeline, exact signatures/indicator state and recovered baseline. Unknown/broadcast target, generic MCE text, indefinite hang, manual intervention inside the protected window, unexplained over-temperature indication, missing evidence or failed restoration is not PASS.
safety_gate: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, independent console and intentional-crash approval.
Preserve baseline logs/settings and prove implicit target before one injection.
Do not reset/power-cycle during the protected autonomous-recovery window.
No automatic retry; escalate on wrong/broadcast target, power/thermal anomaly, timeout or failed boot.
expected_evidence: Harness hash and authoritative implicit-target explanation
Per-target transcript plus synchronized crash/hang/reboot timeline
MCERR/OS-console, BMC catastrophic and recovered UEFI evidence
Recovery, BIOS restoration, health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: After the approved autonomous-reboot wait, preserve evidence and let the qualified owner perform only the documented recovery transition. Verify injector inactivity, platform health and every BIOS setting before any separately authorized next socket or rerun.

source_conflict.reason: Socket 0~N versus parameterless injector, unbounded `eventually`, and unexplained LCD mapping remain unresolved.

blocked.reason: MCERR stimulus and intended response are identifiable; execution is gated on the vendor target semantics, oracle, recovery and FAE.
